affected_boundaries: Compiler and custom adapter subprocess queries

observed_behavior: Valid Gwen compiler inventories exceeded the fixed 30-second budget under concurrent workload; unchanged retries remained indeterminate.
expected_behavior: Callers can select a larger bounded query budget without weakening failure classification.
causal_mechanism: Both subprocess paths used an unchangeable 30000 millisecond timeout.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A workload-dependent resource budget was fixed inside a portable query implementation.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: The caller could not accommodate an observed slower valid compiler query.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Every subprocess has a finite validated caller-selected budget and timeout remains indeterminate.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Propagate --timeout-ms to both subprocess paths, preserving the existing default.

applicability_conditions: Real compiler or adapter queries exceed the default budget
known_non_matches: Compiler errors and malformed adapter responses remain failures regardless of budget
confirmation_evidence: Both query paths used the same fixed constant; controlled hanging subprocesses confirm the override reaches each timeout boundary.
regression_proofs: tests/build-impact.test.js: explicit query budgets retain indeterminate compiler and adapter timeouts
tests/build-impact.test.js: query budgets accept longer bounded waits and reject unbounded or malformed values
